old_problem: The active record kept the case pending for drive/slot identities and expected lane width. pciutils defines exact-BDF verbose enumeration, and the source itself fixes Gen4 16.0 GT/s plus the lane-rate table. The fitted-drive map and per-slot width are normal project configuration, so the review can be complete without guessing them.
disposition_reason: ED-03 permits serial/BDF/slot parameters, ED-04 protects storage identities and forbids mutable namespace assumptions, ED-15 requires the approved per-slot width/downtraining oracle, ED-17 requires bounded logs without clearing, and ED-20 preserves this detection/link test independently of the neighboring firmware update. The source bandwidth table is labeled theoretical rather than a measured performance claim.
decision_basis: Directly read Compatibility row433 all 18 XLSX columns, same-row DeepSeek material, GPT V2/history3024 and adjacent row432 E1.S firmware plus row434 E1.S sensor cases.
Applied pciutils lspci semantics: -D preserves PCI domains, -nn exposes numeric vendor/device IDs, -vvv provides complete parsed capabilities, and -s selects the exact verified BDF.
Preserved Gen4 16.0 GT/s and all source x1/x2/x4/x8/x16 theoretical bandwidth values while separating them from actual workload throughput.
Required a stable serial/model/controller/BDF/root-port/physical-slot join and both LnkCap and LnkSta so simple NVMe enumeration cannot mask downtraining.
Directly read next formal queue Compatibility row434 and verified its manifest identity; no storage, PCIe or DUT action ran.

test_case.test_name: E1.S OS/PCI identity and PCIe Gen4 negotiated speed/lane-width validation
test_case.purpose: Verify every fitted E1.S drive maps to the correct OS, NVMe, PCIe and physical-slot identity and negotiates PCIe Gen4 16.0 GT/s at the project-approved lane width without downtraining or new PCIe errors.
required_package: Approved PCI vendor/device/subsystem IDs for each drive/controller
Per-slot capable and required current PCIe generation/width plus allowed downtraining policy
test_case.test_command: Record a non-destructive log marker and collect complete `lsblk`, `nvme list` and `nvme id-ctrl` identity evidence. Join each serial to its verified controller BDF and physical slot; for every exact BDF and its upstream port capture full `lspci -Dnnvvv -s <BDF>` output. Parse vendor/device/subsystem IDs, LnkCap and LnkSta without discarding the complete blocks. Compare current speed to Gen4 16.0 GT/s and current width to the approved slot width, show the source x1/x2/x4/x8/x16 values only as theoretical line-rate bandwidth, and inspect the bounded AER/kernel/NVMe delta.
test_case.expected_result: Every expected E1.S device is present exactly once and maps consistently across serial, namespace, controller, BDF, root port and physical slot. Numeric PCI IDs match the approved hardware, LnkCap supports the intended link, LnkSta reports 16.0 GT/s at the required lane width, and no unaccepted downtraining, AER or storage error appears.
test_case.pass_fail_basis: PASS requires the approved drive/slot/link matrix, complete identity joins, exact numeric PCI IDs, full LnkCap/LnkSta evidence at 16.0 GT/s and required width, and clean bounded error evidence. NVMe enumeration alone, keyword grep fragments or a theoretical bandwidth number cannot pass. Without the per-slot width/downtraining oracle the result is INCONCLUSIVE—not PASS.
safety_gate: Use read-only lsblk, nvme identify/list and lspci commands only; do not write, reset or benchmark storage
Never infer physical slot or target identity from /dev namespace order or a generic keyword
Capture complete exact-BDF and upstream-port output before extracting fields; do not clear logs
Stop on disappearance, link reset/downtrain or new AER/NVMe error, preserve first evidence and never auto-retry
expected_evidence: Complete lsblk/nvme list/id-ctrl identities and numeric PCI vendor/device/subsystem IDs
Full exact-BDF and upstream lspci blocks with LnkCap/LnkSta
Expected-versus-observed generation/width table and theoretical bandwidth annotation
Bounded AER/kernel/NVMe log delta and engineer verdict
test_case.recovery: The procedure is read-only. On missing device, downtraining or error evidence, stop collection after preserving the first complete identity/path/log bundle, verify the host and unaffected storage remain available, and escalate for a separately approved hardware/link recovery. Do not reset, power-cycle or retry automatically.
